questions.text:
Consider three software items: Program-X, Control Flow Diagram of Program-Y and Control Flow Diagram of Program-Z as shown below

The values of McCabe's Cyclomatic complexity of Program-X, Program-Y, and Program-Z respectively are
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Program X: decisions are if, while and if-else [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 + 1 = 4
- Program Y: 8 nodes, 7 forward edges + 3 back edges = 10 edges [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]-[/latex] 8 + 2 = 4
- Program Z: X followed by Y, joined by one edge [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 + 4 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 7

Answer: 4, 4, 7

questions.text: Consider a software program that is artificially seeded with 100 faults. While testing this program, 159 faults are detected, out of which 75 faults are from those artificially seeded faults. Assuming that both real and seeded faults are of same nature and have same distribution, the estimated number of undetected real faults is ____________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Seeded faults found: 75 of 100 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] detection rate 0.75
- Real faults found: 159 [latex]-[/latex] 75 = 84
- Estimated real faults = 84 / 0.75 = 112

Undetected = 112 [latex]-[/latex] 84 = 28

Answer: 28

questions.text:
Consider a software project with the following information domain characteristics for calculation of function point metric.
Number of external inputs (I) = 30
Number of external outputs (O) = 60
Number of external inquiries (E) = 23
Number of files (F) = 08
Number of external interfaces (N) = 02

It is given that the complexity weighting factors for I, O, E, F and N are 4, 5, 4, 10 and 7, respectively. It is also given that, out of fourteen value adjustment factors that influence the development effort, four factors are not applicable, each of the other four factors have value 3, and each of the remaining factors have value 4. The computed value of function point metric is _____________.
questions.solution:
UFP = 30 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 + 60 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 + 23 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 + 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 + 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 7 = 120 + 300 + 92 + 80 + 14 = 606

Sum of factors = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 0 + 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 + 6 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 36

FP = 606 [latex]\times[/latex] (0.65 + 0.01 [latex]\times[/latex] 36) = 606 [latex]\times[/latex] 1.01 = 612.06

Answer: 612.06

questions.text: Which one of the following assertions concerning code inspection and code walkthrough is true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Inspection is done before unit testing [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 1 false.
- Inspection (formal, checklist based) and walkthrough (informal, led by the author) are different [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 2 false.
- Inspections check against checklists including coding standards [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- Walkthroughs are done by the development team, not an independent test team [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.

Answer: Adherence to coding standards is checked during code inspection

questions.text: Consider the basic COCOMO model where E is the effort applied in person-months, D is the development time in chronological months, KLOC is the estimated number of delivered lines of code (in thousands) and [latex]a_{b},b_{b},c_{b},d_{b}[/latex] have their usual meanings. The basic COCOMO equations are of the form
questions.solution:
Basic COCOMO: effort from size, then time from effort.

[latex]E=a_b(KLOC)^{b_b},\quad D=c_b(E)^{d_b}[/latex]

Answer: E = [latex]a_b[/latex](KLOC)exp([latex]b_b[/latex]), D = [latex]c_b[/latex](E)exp([latex]d_b[/latex])
